title: fix(cli,runner): `objectui generate page` and the core/runner READMEs name the pageType that draws the title; the 11436 pin reads package READMEs and the generator's output (objectui#11450)
body:
Fixes #11450

Clause-②: no

## What changed

A `page` node with no `pageType` is a `record` page. `PageRenderer` leaves a record page's `h1` to a `page:header` block and never draws `title` or `description`. Each producer below wrote a titled page with no `pageType`. Each now names the page type that draws its title.

| Producer | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `objectui generate page NAME` (`generatePage` in `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts`) | `"pageType": "app"`, and the markdown child reads `Welcome to NAME`, not `# Welcome to NAME` | A generated page is a standalone page in an app, the shape PR objectui#11449 gave `examples/hello-world`. With the title drawn, a `#` heading in the markdown would be a second `h1` (see below). |
| `packages/core/README.md` › Type Definitions (`PageNodeSchema` literal) | `pageType: 'app'` | The README's first page node, the same decision PR objectui#11449 made for the docs' first `PageNodeSchema` in `guide/schema-rendering.md`. |
| `packages/runner/README.md` › Example Schema | `"pageType": "home"` | A page titled "Dashboard" whose body is a grid of KPI statistic cards. The spec's `home` is the landing page laid out dashboard-style, and PR objectui#11449 chose `home` for the catalog's "Dashboard" KPI page (`full-dashboard.json`). |
| `packages/runner/src/App.tsx` fallback welcome page | **Deleted** | Unreachable. See below. |

Both values are members of `@objectstack/spec`'s `PageTypeSchema`, which `PageNodeSchema.pageType` takes.

## Measured first, at BASE `5988b6b53`

One-time render probes through the real `SchemaRenderer` with the `@object-ui/components` renderers and plugin-markdown registered, waiting for the lazy markdown module to settle. The probe files were not committed.

- The generator's real output, `{"type":"page","title":"Reports","children":[{"type":"markdown","content":"# Welcome to Reports"}]}`, rendered `data-page-type="record"`. The page drew no `h1` for `Reports`. Once plugin-markdown settled, the markdown child drew one `h1`, `Welcome to Reports`.
- The same document with `"pageType": "app"` drew two `h1`s: `Reports`, then `Welcome to Reports`.
- With `"pageType": "app"` and the markdown text `Welcome to Reports` (no `#`), it drew one `h1`, `Reports`, and the markdown drew a paragraph.
- The same probe on this branch's generator output: one `h1`, `Reports`; the markdown draws a paragraph.

So the card's premise holds for the title: it never drew. "No heading" is true in a host without plugin-markdown, and in a host with it the only heading was the markdown's `Welcome to NAME`. Adding `pageType` alone would have broken the one-page-one-`h1` rule (objectui#3434). That is why the generator's markdown now opens with prose. The built CLI (`node packages/cli/dist/cli.js g page Probe`) writes the new shape.

## `packages/runner/src/App.tsx`: deleted, not fixed

When `loadPage` returned nothing, the code called `setError('Page not found: …')` and then, for `/` only, stored a built-in page titled "Welcome to Object UI" reading `No index page found.`. The render checks `error || !pageSchema` before it reaches `SchemaRenderer`, and the error was always set on that path, so the stored page could never render. Measured at BASE by rendering `RunnerApp` at `/` with a loader that answers `null`, with and without an app config: both drew the 404 block (`404`, `Page not found: /`, `Go Home`), and neither contained `No index page found.`. The same probe after the deletion draws the same thing. The deletion is behaviour-neutral, and it matches the runner README's own account (a missing document "renders as a 404"). Making the page reachable instead would have changed what the runner renders and made that README wrong. ESLint's `no-explicit-any` warning on the deleted `as any` goes with it.

## README population at BASE

Read with the pin's own fence reader over every `packages/**/README.md` (43 tracked files, none generated, none in an ignored directory; 442 fences, 22 that mention `page`): exactly two `type: "page"` object literals, both titled and with no `pageType`, `packages/core/README.md` › Type Definitions and `packages/runner/README.md` › Example Schema. `git grep` for a `type: "page"` key over the same READMEs finds the same two lines. No README declares a page-node interface. There was no third README to fix.

## The pin

`packages/components/src/__tests__/page-node-headings-drawn-11436.test.tsx` now reads two more populations with the same reader and the same assertions:

- every fence of every `README.md` anywhere under `packages/` (a filesystem walk that skips `node_modules`, `dist`, `.turbo` and `coverage` and does enter test directories);
- the page `objectui generate page` writes. The test RUNS the real `generate` into a throwaway directory, with `process.cwd()` stubbed for the one call (the lever the cli test already uses), and reads the file back. It imports the generator's source by relative path, because `@object-ui/cli` publishes its commands only as a bin.

The floor names the three new producers (`packages/core/README.md` › Type Definitions, `packages/runner/README.md` › Example Schema, and the generator). The LIT control requires the README walk to find more than 20 files and 100 fences, and at least one README below a package root. The pin has 66 cases, 6 of them new: a render and a live control for each new producer.

**Where the rendered assertion lives.** This package's `.test.ts` files run in the node-environment `unit` project, which renders nothing. The pin already renders, with the static and live-control legs beside it, so the generator's rendered heading is asserted there. A second renderer in the cli package would be the two-readers shape PR objectui#11449 retired. The cli test keeps the shape: `generate-page-dialect-9847.test.ts` updates its exact scaffold and adds an objectui#11450 case asserting the `pageType` is a drawing member of `PageTypeSchema` and that no markdown child opens an ATX `#` heading. That second half is the one the pin cannot see, because plugin-markdown is not registered in the pin's environment (leg c below).

The ledger row for the pin in `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs` now reads `content/docs/**` and `packages/**`, with the root `README.md` as `notRead` (a bare `README.md` literal resolves against every ancestor directory). `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`: all 114 candidates adjudicated.

## Reverse verification

Every leg ran from committed head `4d90c76e4`, and I wrote each prediction down before the run. Mutations went through objectstack's `ablation-replace.mjs` (its anchors must hit) or a script with an `EXIT INT TERM` trap and absolute paths. Each restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- **(a)** The three producer files restored to BASE (`generate.ts` and both READMEs; blob == BASE blob for each), the new tests unchanged. Predicted 9 failed / 60 passed. Got **9 failed / 60 passed**:
  - pin: the record-page check, three renders, three live controls;
  - cli: the 9847 scaffold and the new objectui#11450 case.
- **(b)** Deleted only the `pageType: "app",` line in `generate.ts` (anchor 1 → 0). Predicted 5 failed / 64 passed. Got **5 failed / 64 passed**: the record check, the generator's render and live control, and the two cli cases.
- **(c)** Put the `# ` back in the generated markdown (anchor 1 → 0, replacement 0 → 1). Predicted 2 failed / 67 passed, with the pin green. Got **2 failed / 67 passed**, both in the cli test. The pin cannot see a second `h1` drawn by plugin-markdown, and the cli assertion is what catches it.
- **(d)** Pointed the README walk at `README.mdx`, so it finds nothing. Predicted 2 failed / 63 passed of 65, the four README cases gone. Got **2 failed / 63 passed (65)**: the LIT control and the floor.
- **(e)** Ledger control: with `packages/**` and the `notRead` entry dropped from the row, `--audit` exits 1 with 5 `unadjudicated-document` findings naming the pin.
- **(f)** `check:doc-snippets` compiles the core README block: with `pageType: 'detail'` there it reports `TS2322: Type '"detail"' is not assignable to type 'PageType | undefined'` at that block, 776 judged and 1 failed.

## Tests and gates (head `ea95fb6e7`)

- Vitest from the worktree root, 27 files and 1081 tests passed: the pin; the cli files `generate-page-dialect-9847.test.ts` and `app-generator.test.ts`; all six `packages/runner` test files; `guide-schema-rendering-data-context-8021.test.tsx`; `scripts/__tests__/markdown-test-inputs.test.ts` and the eight other `scripts/__tests__` files that import or name it; and the eight further `scripts/__tests__` files the ledger records as readers of the two edited READMEs.
- `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/components^...' --filter='@object-ui/cli^...' --filter='@object-ui/runner^...' --concurrency=2`: 14 successful. Then the `check:doc-snippets --build-filter` closure: 35 successful.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` exits 0 at this head. `@object-ui/cli` and `@object-ui/runner` `type-check` exit 0 at `4d90c76e4`, and neither package changed after it. `--listFilesOnly` puts the cli test in the cli program, and the pin plus `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts` in the components test program.
- `pnpm check:doc-snippets`: 776 of 776 blocks judged, 0 failed.
- Each of these exits 0 with its own verdict line: `check:readme-exports` (43 READMEs), `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-fences`, `changeset:check`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` (2 changesets declared), and `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 9 paths: NOT GOVERNED, an ordinary pull request.
- ESLint `--no-inline-config --format json` over the 5 changed lintable files: 5 files, 0 errors, 1 warning. The warning is `react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization` on `App.tsx`'s `loader` `useMemo`, which BASE has too. The narrowing holds:
  - `--print-config` gives 116 to 119 rules for the four TypeScript files and 0 for `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs`. JSON and markdown files have no ESLint config.
  - `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem (both greps exit 1, against a control grep that hits). So no verdict on an untouched file can move.

Changesets: `@object-ui/cli` patch (the generator) and `@object-ui/runner` patch (`App.tsx`). The README edits need none: the presence gate subtracts `*.md` from published files.

NOT MEASURED, a declared narrowing: the whole `packages/components` and `packages/cli` suites, and the repo-wide `pnpm lint`. CI runs them.
- Patch round 2 (head `38629a052`, after merging `origin/main` `6007dd4e4`): `scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts` no longer lists `packages/runner/src/App.tsx` among the producers objectui#7181 migrated, because this PR deletes the fallback page that entry pinned. With the entry put back, the census fails exactly as CI did (`expected ... to contain 'children:'`, 1 failed / 21 passed). The 44 test files that read a changed file (1805 tests) pass on the merged head.

## Acceptance notes

- **The docs page that described the deleted placeholder is corrected (patch round 1).** `content/docs/utilities/runner.mdx` said twice that, with no metadata, `/` shows "the built-in `No index page found.` placeholder". Both sentences now say `/` renders the 404 block, `Page not found: /`. Measured with the real `LocalBundleLoader` and no `src/app-data`: `RunnerApp` at `/` draws `404`, `Page not found: /` and `Go Home`. The 18 tests the ledger records as readers of `runner.mdx` pass at `ccd5d34f1`.
- **`objectui generate --output DIR` is ignored.** The CLI declares `--output` ("Output directory for generated schemas", default `schemas/`), and `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx` lists it. The action never passes it to `generate`. Measured with the built CLI: `g page Probe --output custom/` wrote `pages/probe.json` and no `custom/` directory. That is a different defect from this card, so it is not fixed here.
- Not filed: on a 404 at `/`, the runner's `Go Home` button navigates to `/`, the page it is already on.

Concurrency: `main` gained objectui#11460, objectui#11461 and objectui#11462 after BASE. None touches these files. objectui#11460 edits `packages/layout/README.md`, which the widened pin now reads. It holds no page node on the new tip (grep exit 1; the same file has 15 `type` lines).
